source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Corvette Body, p.1B-30

procedures.title: Dents or pits in panels, cracks in glaze coat
steps: Fill the flaws using the plastic solder repair described earlier.
Feather-sand the area with No. 220 paper and finish with No. 320.
Prepare the area for paint refinishing.

procedures.title: Cracked panels
steps: Saw along the break line with a hacksaw blade and remove the broken section (see figure 65 in the manual).
Strip paint down to the plastic on both pieces using Lacquer Remover or equivalent.
On the underside of both pieces, thoroughly remove dirt and deadener for about 2 to 3 inches back from the break, then remove paint and scuff for a good bond.
Remove all cracked or fractured material along the break, bevel the mating edges to about 30 degrees with a file or grinder, and scuff the plastic along the edges.
Mask surrounding panels with non-staining tape.
Align the two pieces with C clamps, leaving roughly 1/8 inch between them or whatever gap gives correct alignment (see figure 66 in the manual).
Cut two backup pieces of woven glass fiber cloth large enough to overlap the break by about 2 inches.
Clean the repair area with Prep-Sol, then a tack rag.
Apply the resin repair procedure described earlier.
notes: Sometimes extra reinforcement along the fracture helps (continued next page).
Figure 50 on this page shows the body mounts (No. 1 to No. 4) with bolt, washer, cushions, shim, nut and access cover.
